name: Urea
notes: Split application recommended; loss by volatilization if surface applied

name: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate)
notes: Best applied at sowing; do not mix with urea

name: MOP (Muriate of Potash)
notes: Avoid on saline soils; split for sandy soils

name: SSP (Single Super Phosphate)
notes: Good source of sulphur too; apply as basal dose

name: NPK 17-17-17
notes: Balanced fertilizer for most crops; common complex

name: NPK 10-26-26
notes: High P and K; good for root and fruit development

name: NPK 20-20-0
notes: Suitable where K is sufficient in soil

name: Ammonium Sulphate
notes: Good for alkaline soils; contains sulphur

name: Zinc Sulphate (ZnSO4)
notes: Apply once in 2-3 years as basal; foliar spray for quick correction

name: Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4)
notes: Foliar spray more effective than soil application

name: Manganese Sulphate
notes: Apply when pH > 7.5 soils show Mn deficiency

name: Borax
notes: Critical for groundnut and sunflower; deficiency causes hollow heart

name: FYM (Farm Yard Manure)
notes: C:N ratio 30:1; apply 2-3 weeks before planting

name: Vermicompost
notes: Higher nutrient content than FYM; apply 2-4 weeks before planting

name: Green Manure (Dhaincha)
notes: Sesbania aculeata is best; fixes N and improves soil structure

name: Neem Cake
notes: Also acts as neem-coated urea when mixed; nitrification inhibitor

name: Rhizobium
notes: Legume-specific; do not mix with chemical fertilizers or fungicides

name: Azospirillum
notes: Free-living N-fixer for cereals and grasses; saves 25% N fertilizer

name: Phosphobacteria (PSB)
notes: Solubilizes bound phosphorus; saves 25-30% P fertilizer

name: Potassium Mobilizing Bacteria (KMB)
notes: Mobilizes fixed K; saves 20% K fertilizer input

name: VAM (Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhizae)
notes: Enhances P and micronutrient uptake; improves drought tolerance

name: Trichoderma
notes: Also controls soil-borne diseases (root rot / wilt)

name: Pseudomonas fluorescens
notes: Controls bacterial blight and wilt diseases

name: Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate)
notes: Essential for groundnut pod filling; corrects soil salinity

name: Lime (Agricultural)
notes: Corrects soil acidity; raises pH; apply 1 month before planting
